# `css/no-unused-classes`

**A class a global stylesheet declares is used by a file that loads it**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-css` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-css` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | CSS, SCSS |
| **Turned on by** | `codelaw:css/project` at `warn` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `warn` |
| **Options** | none — severity only |
| **Fix** | `suggest` — `codelaw fix --unsafe` applies it; review the diff, it can change behaviour (a class can be built at run time or used by markup outside the repo, so deleting its rule needs a person to accept the diff) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.5.2 |
| **Scope** | project — reads the whole repository through the project graph, not one file at a time |
| **Ported from** | `biome/nursery/noUnusedClasses` |

## What it checks

Every class a global stylesheet declares is written by some JavaScript, TypeScript or HTML file that loads with it: a file whose entries reach the stylesheet (the file imports it, an importer does, a page links it, or another stylesheet `@import`s it). Behaviour of Biome's `noUnusedClasses`, read from its documentation and rewritten.

**Why:** a class nobody writes is dead CSS every page downloads, and it hides the classes the markup really uses.

A word counts as a use wherever a file writes it: a string, a template, an attribute value (`className`, `class`, `classList.add`, a library's prop), and `@apply` or `composes` in a stylesheet. The static start of a name built at run time (`btn-${size}`) keeps every class that begins with it. A stylesheet nothing loads is left alone, and so is one the rule cannot read whole (a class named by interpolation), an entry point and anything in `[graph] keep`. A CSS Module is not a global stylesheet: its classes are judged by `css-modules/no-unused-class`.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-css
pip install codelaw-rules-css
```

**Then extend a preset that turns it on** — `codelaw:css/project` sets it to `warn`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:css/project"]
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"css/no-unused-classes" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — a scope of your own needs `files`:

```toml
[scope.legacy]
files = ["src/legacy/**/*.css"]
rules = { "css/no-unused-classes" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"css/no-unused-classes" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"css/no-unused-classes" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"css/no-unused-classes" = { severity = "warn" }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "css/no-unused-classes": {"severity": "warn"}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **CSS:** `/* codelaw-ignore css/no-unused-classes: <reason> */`
- **SCSS:** `// codelaw-ignore css/no-unused-classes: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `/* codelaw-ignore css/no-unused-classes expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason> */`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule css/no-unused-classes --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain css/no-unused-classes       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule css/no-unused-classes  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>         # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## How to fix

1. Search for the class: a name built at run time counts only through its static start.
2. If markup outside the repo uses it, add the stylesheet to `[graph] keep`.
3. Otherwise delete the rule (`codelaw fix --unsafe` does it when the class is the rule's only selector).

## Examples

### CSS

#### Don't

```css files
/* src/styles.css */
.card { padding: 1rem; }
.legacy { color: red; }
// src/Card.jsx
import "./styles.css";
export const Card = () => <div className="card" />;
```

#### Do

```css files
/* src/styles.css */
.card { padding: 1rem; }
// src/Card.jsx
import "./styles.css";
export const Card = () => <div className="card" />;
```

### SCSS

#### Don't

```scss files
/* src/styles.scss */
.card { padding: 1rem; }
.legacy { color: red; }
// src/Card.jsx
import "./styles.scss";
export const Card = () => <div className="card" />;
```

#### Do

```scss files
/* src/styles.scss */
.card { padding: 1rem; }
// src/Card.jsx
import "./styles.scss";
export const Card = () => <div className="card" />;
```

## Differences from the source

Biome's `noUnusedClasses` reads the files that import one stylesheet. This rule reads what loads with it through the project graph, so a class used by any file under the same entry counts. `graph/no-unused-css-classes` (purgecss) counts a word written anywhere in the project; this one counts only files the stylesheet loads with, so two apps in one repository are judged apart.
